note: Real projects at a pinned commit, with answers somebody checked by hand. Run with `npm run corpus`. A number that moves is not automatically a bug - a real fix moves numbers - but it must be re-verified and explained, never recorded blindly. `verified` says how each one was checked; an expectation with no verification behind it is not evidence, it is what the tool said that day.

repos.name: keycloak
repos.why: Red Hat's identity server - the login layer inside banks, insurers and governments. Java, Liquibase and a React admin UI on PatternFly, which is three stacks in one repository.

checks.verified: 2026-10-12. All 77 never-runs read by hand - 31 @Ignore, 21 @Disabled, 19 .skip, 6 confirmed with grep. The single swallows-failure is genuine and is a real defect in Red Hat's admin client: authenticationManagement.spec.ts `try { await getConfig(id); fail('should not find deleted config'); } catch {}` - a bare catch in TypeScript catches everything, including what fail() throws, so the test passes whether or not the config was deleted. It must stay 1 and it must stay that test. Phase 43 shipped 166 here, all the Java expected-exception idiom, which cannot swallow an AssertionError; two more were found and removed in Phase 44, where the empty catch guarded setup and the assertions came after it. unfinished-expectation and tautology are 0 and that is the guard, not an absence.

2026-10-12. 293 findings. The destructive ones were counted independently with grep across the 83 changelogs and match exactly: 67 dropColumn + 39 renameColumn = 106 breaks-old-code, 25 dropTable = destroys-data. filesRead is 89 rather than the 83 changelogs because six real .sql init scripts are read too, correctly reporting nothing. locks-writes was 196 and is 162: the 34 that went were indexes built on tables created in the same changeSet, which hold no rows, and a script confirmed none of the 162 that remain is on a table created in its own file. That suppression existed from Phase 33 and had never worked for Liquibase, because it knew only SQL's CREATE TABLE and not <createTable tableName="...">.

2026-10-12: all 5 barriers opened and read in the source. Two are real defects in Red Hat's production interface - an unlabelled in the account console users see, and a bare in the admin theme editor. The other three are a missing alt and two elements with no lang.

repos.name: openmrs-core
repos.why: A real hospital system. Java and Liquibase, and the second JVM project in the corpus - one sample of a language is not a measurement.

checks.verified: 2026-10-12. 39 never-runs and 1 tautology checked against the source: 37 carry @Disabled or @Ignore directly, VisitValidatorTest has @Disabled after a three-line comment, CreateConceptDictionaryDataSet is disabled at class level, and the tautology is StartModuleAnnotationReuseTest.shouldPass, which is assertTrue(true) and nothing else. swallows-failure is 0, correcting Phase 42, which recorded 2 here as genuine: both are `try { ...; fail(); } catch (Exception e) {}`, which fails properly on the JVM. tautology was 2 until RefByUuidTest was re-read - its assertTrue(true) sits beside a fail() in the catch, so the test can fail. These counts are from after line endings were normalised on read; before that they differed between Windows and Linux.

repos.name: bitwarden-server
repos.why: Enterprise password management: the .NET stack that insurance and banking back offices run on. C# with xUnit, 456 EF Core migrations beside 1,264 T-SQL files, and Razor views - three dialects Tewip had never been measured against.

checks.verified: 2026-10-12. 43 never-runs, matching an independent grep for [Fact(Skip= and [Theory(Skip= exactly. swallows-failure is 0 and that is correct rather than missed: bitwarden's test suite contains no empty catch block at all, checked with grep. That is the measurement Phase 43 shipped as an assumption - C# was deliberately excluded from the JVM rule because NUnit, xUnit and MSTest all throw assertion failures deriving from Exception, so catch (Exception) really does swallow them there. If swallows-failure stops being 0, read the new ones. never-runs was 1 before this trial: xUnit's skip attribute was unknown, and the one finding it did have was `collections.Skip(1).ToList()`, which is LINQ.

2026-10-12. 558 findings, down from 919, with 361 false positives removed and every survivor checked. locks-writes was 714: no table was recognised as freshly created, because the pattern read PostgreSQL's "quoted" form but not SQL Server's [dbo].[Grant], and knew no framework's way of saying it - so EF Core's CreateTable followed by CreateIndex, which is what Prisma does, counted every index as blocking writes. All 339 EF Core locks-writes that remain were confirmed by script to be on tables not created in the same migration, and the src/Sql/dbo/Tables definitions now report none at all.

2026-10-12. 251 findings, down from 374. The 111 input-label barriers that went were ASP.NET Core Tag Helpers: asp-for="Name" renders for="Name" on the label and id="Name" on the input, so the association is real and simply not written here. The 3 input-label that remain were opened and read - two labels carrying neither for nor asp-for, and one input whose only description is a placeholder, which is not a label. The link-name findings are genuine: social icon links in the email templates whose only content is an , so a screen reader announces 'link' and nothing else.

repos.name: saleor
repos.why: Commerce, and the largest Python test suite in the corpus. Phase 42 verified it by hand and the numbers then lived only in a commit message.

checks.verified: 2026-10-12. Zero accusations across 12,982 tests - no tautology, no unfinished expectation, no swallowed failure, nothing skipped - and that agrees with the hand verification in Phase 42, which read the condemned list and found it empty. The four zeros are the measurement here: Saleor is the largest Python suite in the corpus and the one most likely to surface a false accusation, so any of them moving off zero needs reading before it is believed.

repos.name: firefly-iii
repos.why: A real finance application, and the only Laravel project in the corpus. Phase 41 taught `schema` to read its 61 migrations; nothing has held that in place since.

checks.verified: 2026-10-12. 61 migrations read, which is the number Phase 41 established by hand after Laravel was added as a dialect - it had been 0. This entry exists to hold that: Laravel is the only PHP dialect in the corpus, and its rollback is commonly written above the forward path, which is the shape that made it worth testing at all.
